sources.title: GTA 6 Launch Trailer Teases Jason's Troubled Past, a Steamy Shower Scene With Lucia, and Much More
sources.text: Rockstar has released the launch trailer for GTA 6 , which shows us brand new footage of Jason and Lucia as well as the open world. The trailer, which weighs in at 1:30, touches on Jason's troubled past, which involved leaving the army not on the best of terms. We see snippets of a steamy shower scene with Lucia, who is wearing an ankle tag, and plenty of explosive open-world action. Rather than showing gameplay, the launch trailer showcases cinematic action in GTA 6 as it nears its November 19 launch. As per Rockstar's partnership with Sony, the PS5 is prominent in the trailer, with the "plays best on PS5" message displayed at the start. The trailer confirms the footage was "captured on PS5." The trailer begins with some narration from Jason. "I got in some trouble in the army," he begins. "Didn't leave on the best of terms. They don't give loans or anything to people like me." We see a bearded Jason working at Brian's Marina, buffing a boat before he receives a call from Lucia Caminos. Presumably this is the call Jason gets to pick up Lucia from prison. We're shown what look like flashbacks to Jason's time in the army, where he appears to have been in the special forces. We see him wading through water as part of a military unit, and leaping out of a helicopter while on some sort of mission. But these scenes could easily be set in the "present," rather than the past, with Jason gearing up for, perhaps, a police operation. Either way, it explains why Jason is so handy with a gun. We're then treated to various shots showing Jason and Lucia getting up to no good across Vice City, with glimpses of that steamy shower scene. The shot of Lucia wearing an ankle tag could hint at initial restrictions to exploration, as more of the world is opened up during progression through the story, but that's speculation. This week, we learnt about GTA 6's sweat system, and there's a shot in the launch trailer that looks to show this in action. We see a man working out, and he's putting a lot of effort in. Sweat? Yep, it's all there. "Are we gonna be okay?" Lucia asks Jason after yet more explosive shots. "We stuck together through everything," Jason replies. "Just gotta get through it." Here's the official blurb from Rockstar on the GTA 6 launch trailer: We also have confirmation that electronic duo Justice composed the original score for GTA 6. Indeed their track, Flower in a Hurricane, featuring fellow Grammy-winners Tame Impala and SZA along with King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard, plays during the launch trailer. It's been a busy week for GTA 6. We've got a report on what sounds like the end of Cyberleek , details of GTA 6’s sweat system , and confirmation GTA 6 is eligible for The Game Awards 2026 . sources.text: We've put together over 30 screenshots from the GTA 6 launch trailer, showing off Rockstar's open-world in detail. Rockstar surprised fans this morning by dropping a new trailer for GTA 6 . This appears to be the final full trailer for the game before launch, but it paints a picture of the thrilling story. The new trailer highlights some of the more romantic and steamy moments between Jason and Lucia alongside major action setpieces, including one where someone dangles off a payload that is being flown across Vice City. It's pretty over the top, but in all of the right ways. We've put together a slideshow of some of the key images from the trailer, allowing you to take in some details you may have missed, such as the fact that Jason has a dog with him during one of his helicopter rides. You can take a look at the new images down below. Remember, the GTA 6 launch trailer was entirely captured in-game from a PS5, so what you're seeing here is how the game will run on base PS5, not the PS5 Pro. We're yet to see the game running on the Xbox Series X and S. Here's the official blurb from Rockstar on the GTA 6 launch trailer: We are just a little over 30 days away from launch and less than a month away from being able to pre-load GTA 6. Rockstar Games has confirmed that players will be able to pre-download the game starting on November 12, ensuring you'll be fully prepared for the game's release as soon as it becomes available. Despite this seemingly being the final trailer, GTA 6 will still have plenty of marketing beats between now and launch. It's been a busy month GTA 6. Rockstar has been taking over Miami with murals, blimps, and signange . It is even preparing to re-decorate Miami Beach with GTA 6-themed items, such as umbrellas. On November 18, the NBA will host a GTA 6-themed regular season game in Miami with a Vice City themed court, jerseys, and in-person activations . No expense has been spared in marketing this game and we're likely going to see a bunch of other marketing beats in the coming weeks. Meanwhile, we've got a report on what sounds like the end of Cyberleek , details of GTA 6’s sweat system , and confirmation GTA 6 is eligible for The Game Awards 2026 . GTA 6 will finally release on November 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S. A PC release is also rumored for early 2027 . Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

sources.text: Yet another look at GTA 6 has come our way, which means it’s time to get forensic; we’ve gone through the new trailer with a fine-tooth comb to pick out all of the interesting details hidden within. From peeks at what’s in store for some of its most explosive missions, further insights into Jason’s military past, and more than one visit to a steamy shower, there’s plenty of new things to take a look at. Let’s not waste any more time. Here are the 33 details we spotted in the GTA 6 launch trailer. Multiple shots offer a closer look at Jason and paint a pretty clear picture of the kind of man we’ll be taking control of. We already knew that he was ex-military, but midway through the trailer we see him wearing a U.S. Army T-shirt that offers more details on his service. 1. Firstly, the combat training school Jason seemingly trained at is located in North Fort Law. Longtime fans will recognise this as the military base from the very first Grand Theft Auto game. In that original game, it was located in the state of New Guernsey, but it’s more likely that the one Jason attended is in the State of Alderney, the HD universe’s take on New Jersey. We know that Lucia is from Liberty City, which is located in the neighboring State of Liberty – perhaps they met when Jason was stationed at the base? 2. More prominent than that small print is the word “Marauder,” which matches the skull-and-parachute tattoo on Jason’s arm that we’ve seen in previous videos. The Marauders are presumably the unit he served in, and may be a reference to the real-life Merrill's Marauders, a 1940s special forces group. Its modern-day equivalent is the 75th Ranger Regiment, and so it’s likely that Jason was a ranger. 3. It seems like Jason has fallen on tough times since he left the forces. “I got in some trouble in the army, didn’t leave on the best of terms,” he says in the trailer’s opening. “They don’t give loans, anything, to people like me.” With a situation like that, it’s no wonder Jason has resorted to crime. The cost of living is only going up! 4. Thankfully, it seems like Jason’s experience in the Marauders has equipped him with all the tools for a very fruitful life of crime. We see him wading through water dressed in special forces-like infiltration gear, a pair of night-vision goggles on his head and a silenced assault rifle in his hands. He’s accompanied by two other men, and the trio seem to have disembarked from a boat. While the blush night sky certainly looks very Floridian (or should we say Leonidan), an odd reptile to the left of the scene appears to be a komodo dragon, which is native to Indonesia. Is this a flashback to a mission from Jason’s army days? Or is the reptile simply a native of Leonida’s wetlands, and Jason has perhaps called on some former squadmates to help with some kind of job? 5. Much of the criminal work we see committed across this trailer has something of a military feel to it. We later see Jason on a helicopter, dressed in a bulletproof vest and demonstrating a very professional demeanor. He’s joined by a dog, potentially pointing to not just Jason having a pet, but also being able to use them as some kind of working dog. Later shots also show Jason confidently disembarking a chopper and checking the chambered round in his rifle – all small details, but ones that help paint the picture of a deeply competent professional. 6. Lucia may not have Jason’s highly trained background, but it looks like she’ll eventually adopt at least some of his tactics. A minute into the trailer, we can see her dressed in special forced black and equipped with a Shrewsbury rotary grenade launcher, popping explosives into pursuing police vehicles. 7. She’s demolishing those cars from on high, hanging from the side of some kind of cargo net. A few seconds later, we see a helicopter carrying a giant load in a very similar cargo net – it seems likely that these shots are taken from the same mission, and that Lucia will hang from the net before or after it’s been dragged through the side of a skyscraper. 8. The damage caused by the crash is more detailed than anything we’ve seen in prior GTA games, with hundreds of shards of glass erupting from the side of the building. While this shot alone is far from confirmation that the game will feature Battlefield-like destruction tech, it is a flashy insight into just how detailed Rockstar is able to make environmental demolition. 9. That kind of collateral damage is to be expected from crime on the scale that GTA typically depicts, and it seems like this game has no intention of being smaller than GTA 5’s biggest moments. We can see Lucia leaping off a car onto a commercial liner, suggesting something on the same scale as some of Trevor’s airborne antics. This shot is likely the precursor to the scene in the second trailer that shows Lucia fighting in a plane’s hold as its landing gear deploys. 10. The aforementioned chopper mission is probably a heist, but what’s definitely a heist is the bank job we see. This is actually the vault we previously saw in a screenshot we exclusively debuted back in August , complete with the burning bank notes and Lucia with her hair in a ponytail. 11. For that shot, Lucia is joined not by Jason but by another anonymous character. We can’t see their face, but whoever they are, it looks like we won’t be alone when conducting heists. In a later shot we see Lucia accompanied by gunmen disguised as construction workers, suggesting we’ll often be joined by crews of criminals. But will these be supporting characters introduced as part of the story, or NPCs hired to help, akin to how heist crews worked in GTA 5? 12. sources.text: A “launch” trailer a month before launch. A “launch” trailer a month before launch. The day is almost here, as Grand Theft Auto VI is just about a month away from finally coming out. But before that there’s still one more look from Rockstar Games, which just put out a brief “launch” trailer for the game. It doesn’t reveal much new, but the 90 second clip does give a good sense of the Miami-inflected vibe. It also includes a new track from electronic duo Justice , who are scoring the game. (As with past titles, GTA VI has a huge focus on music .) Rockstar says the new trailer was captured entirely on a PS5. The trailer also includes a brief new description for the game’s story, for those who haven’t been following along closely: Jason and Lucia have always known the deck is stacked against them. But when an easy score goes wrong, they find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida — forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive. Of course, if you’re looking for more in-depth gameplay, Rockstar dropped a lengthy “extended look” back in August , which showed off just how cinematic the experience is shaping up to be . Meanwhile, leaks from the game have continued to propagate on the internet, revealing some of the more, let’s say, sensitive elements of the experience . Grand Theft Auto VI launches on November 19th on the PS5 and Xbox, a solid 13 years after the last GTA — though we might not have to wait quite that long for its inevitable sequel .

sources.title: GTA 6 launch trailer shows a more intimate Jason and Lucia as fans struggle to believe it's real
sources.text: New Grand Theft Auto 6 launch trailer really makes it feel real – we made it The GTA 6 launch trailer is here, formally ushering in the next era of Grand Theft Auto after more than a decade post-GTA 5. Rockstar shared the new trailer earlier today, "featuring the debut of 'Flower in a Hurricane' from original score composers Justice feat. Tame Impala, SZA, and King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard," and confirming that this song will appear on the official GTA 6 soundtrack album. The short trailer sees the dual protagonists, Jason and Lucia, open up about their struggles. Jason notably sports long hair for much of the trailer; in the opening seconds, he discusses the obstacles he's faced after a less-than-glamorous military departure. Lucia is seen sporting a monitoring anklet during an intimate shower scene, and at one point wonders, "Are we gonna be OK" amid a storm of crime. Rockstar was in a very helicopter mood with this trailer. One helicopter crashes behind an assault rifle-toting Jason, Lucia rides another through the streets with a grenade launcher in hand, and in a third sequence a chopper is shown carrying a chained load of (presumably stolen) cargo through the city like a wrecking ball, shattering a row of windows on another building. A once-again short-haired Jason emerges from a helicopter in the next shot, only to cut to him and Lucia jumping off a roof into some sort of hotel pool. "Jason and Lucia have always known the deck is stacked against them," reads the video description. "But when an easy score goes wrong, they find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida — forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive." The early response from Grand Theft Auto fans is unsurprisingly enormous, with millions piling into Rockstar's accounts across social media. The trailer crossed 1 million views on YouTube in about half an hour, if you can trust overwhelmed metrics. In the comments, GTA 6 hopefuls express disbelief at finally having a launch trailer in their hands. "I thought I would never live this moment," reads one top comment. "We are really at the finish line!!!" says another fan. Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more Grand Theft Auto 6 is out November 19 on PS5 and Xbox Series X. The launch trailer was captured on PS5, with a clear PlayStation marketing push bookending it. As if you needed another reminder of why GTA 6 took so long, it has a realistic sweat system that makes Jason and Lucia perspire based on how hard they dance . sources.title: Some great games to play before GTA VI and Zelda launch
sources.text: Eight new releases including old-school horror, laid-back dressmaking, and the return of Castlevania. You could say we’re in the eye of the storm right now. The storm, of course, being the fall and winter release calendar for new video games. Things started out with a hectic few weeks that were packed with major titles like Control Resonant , Marvel’s Wolverine , Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave , and Gears of War: E-Day . Meanwhile, next month will be dedicated almost entirely to two gigantic games: Nintendo’s remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time and the long-anticipated Grand Theft Auto VI . But even though things are comparatively quiet at the moment, there are still a handful of great games that have come out recently. Even better: Many of them are short enough that you can easily squeeze them in before your life is taken over by Hyrule and Vice City. Here are eight titles you can check out before things get overwhelming again. Available on the PS5, Xbox, Switch, and Steam. This new Castlevania game from the studios that worked on Dead Cells has everything I could have hoped for: intricate levels, challenging platforming, tough bosses, and secrets upon secrets to discover. Sometimes, the game got a little too tough, but thanks to some generous assist settings, I could tweak the experience to be exactly what I wanted it to be. Belmont’s Curse whips. —JP South African developer Free Lives — known for decidedly not-cozy games like Broforce and Genital Jousting — has ventured into the “cozy” space with Dressmaker , a game about designing and sewing dresses, via a small internal team dubbed Cozy Lives. From your small village shop, you take commissions, sketch designs, pick fabrics and accessories, cut the dress patterns, pin them on a mannequin, and sew it all together. There is a lot of creative freedom. You could certainly spend dozens of hours meticulously designing and accessorizing your dresses — I definitely have — but you can also play in relaxed half-hour sessions when inspiration strikes, making it a flexible option in a pretty packed season for games. —KP Available on the Xbox, PlayStation, Switch, and PC. Resident Evil and Silent Hill are as big as they’ve ever been , but if you’re looking for that old-school survival horror vibe, Heartworm is the game. It looks and plays like a long-lost PlayStation classic — you even have limited inventory — albeit with some optional concessions for modern players, like getting rid of the dreaded tank controls. It also has an interesting twist as your character carries around a camera that serves as both a flashlight and a weapon, giving the game its own distinct-yet-familiar feel. —AW As far as co-op puzzle-solving goes, Orbitals doesn’t reinvent the wheel. But it nails the fundamentals, and it does so in a pitch-perfect ’90s anime package that elevates it beyond a stock puzzle adventure. The world and character designs are reminiscent of the peak Toonami days — the timeless art of Akira Toriyama or the stylish sci-fi of Cowboy Bebop — and are gorgeous even if you aren’t particularly nostalgic for the era . It’s short enough to finish in a few sessions, and because Orbitals comes with a “friend pass” that allows someone else to play with you without buying their own copy, it’s easy to get a friend to join you for the journey. —KP Available on the PS5, Xbox, Switch 2, and PC. This is a game best explained in relation to things that already exist. It has the 2D exploration of Metroid , controls like a point-and-click adventure, the slow-burning survival horror of early Silent Hill and Resident Evil , and a weirdo Americana vibe that’s clearly inspired by Twin Peaks . That may sound derivative, but Silver Pines is unlike anything I’ve ever played, a detective story that’s a mix of straight-up terror and deliberate and methodical exploration. It even makes you spend (fictional) money to save your game and you can relax with a cup of coffee to increase your stamina. —AW Toem 2 is a sequel to 2021’s black-and-white indie game about photography , and it’s just as lovely as the original. The characters are charming, the quests are silly, and taking pictures is a snap. It was a great travel companion during a recent trip, especially because I was able to finish it over the course of a couple hours. —JP Available on the PS5, Xbox, Switch, and Steam. For those interested in video game history, any game with the Digital Eclipse name on it is worth checking out. Even still, a Toy Story collection doesn’t seem as immediately interesting as, say, a history of Karateka or Tetris . But through some fascinating archival material coupled with the actual games, the collection makes it clear how technically ambitious these games were, from squeezing 3D sprites on the Sega Genesis to a surprisingly open-ended A Bug’s Life adventure. Just as important, they’re still fun to play. —AW Available on the PS5, Xbox, Switch, and PC. In Well Dweller , an indie Metroidvania from developer Kyle Thompson, you play as an adorable bird in a world filled with cute characters and alarmingly grotesque bosses. The zones are weird and memorable, like a docks level where you jump from dead fish hanging in nets, but they’re a blast to explore, especially because Glimmer’s matchstick weapon cleverly serves double duty as a springboard you can stick to walls. Well Dweller came out of nowhere for me, and it’s easily become one of my favorites of the year. —JP

sources.text: A Rockstar Games surpreendeu os fãs nesta quinta-feira (15) com a divulgação de um novo trailer de lançamento de Grand Theft Auto VI ( GTA 6 ) . Publicado sem aviso prévio, o vídeo apresenta novas cenas da história, sequências de ação e detalhes sobre o relacionamento entre os protagonistas Jason e Lucia. O lançamento está previsto para 19 de novembro de 2026 , no PlayStation 5 e nos consoles Xbox Series X e Series S. Com a estreia se aproximando, a Rockstar intensifica a divulgação de um dos jogos mais aguardados dos últimos anos. Entre as novidades do vídeo está uma explicação sobre o passado de Jason. O protagonista revela que enfrentou problemas durante sua passagem pelo Exército e deixou a instituição em circunstâncias desfavoráveis. Segundo o personagem, essa situação dificultou seu acesso a empréstimos e outras oportunidades financeiras, sugerindo que suas dificuldades econômicas podem ter contribuído para seu envolvimento com o crime. O trailer também apresenta perseguições de veículos, tiroteios e outras atividades criminosas, elementos tradicionais da franquia. Outro destaque é o relacionamento entre Jason e Lucia. As novas cenas mostram momentos de intimidade do casal, indicando que a relação terá espaço importante na narrativa. A trilha sonora também ganhou novidades. O vídeo apresenta a música Flower in a Hurricane , do duo eletrônico Justice, com participações de Tame Impala, SZA e King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard. Segundo as informações divulgadas, a faixa integrará a trilha sonora oficial do jogo. Além do novo trailer, GTA 6 está dentro do período de elegibilidade do The Game Awards 2026, uma das principais premiações da indústria de games. De acordo com as regras divulgadas pela organização, os jogos precisam estar disponíveis comercialmente até 20 de novembro de 2026, às 21h, no horário do Pacífico , para participar das categorias principais. Como o lançamento de GTA 6 está marcado para 19 de novembro, o título atende ao prazo estabelecido, desde que a data seja mantida. O jogo poderá ser considerado em categorias como Melhor Direção, Melhor Narrativa, Melhor Direção de Arte, Melhor Trilha Sonora e Jogo do Ano. Entretanto, a elegibilidade não garante uma indicação. A seleção dos concorrentes dependerá da avaliação do júri responsável pela premiação. Caso seja indicado, GTA 6 poderá disputar espaço com outros lançamentos de 2026, incluindo Resident Evil Requiem , Control Resonant e Forza Horizon 6 . Com pouco mais de um mês até sua estreia, o novo trailer representa mais uma etapa da campanha de divulgação da Rockstar e oferece aos jogadores mais uma visão adicional da história que será apresentada na sequência. sources.title: Hearing That Dude Say ‘Grand Theft Auto’ At The End Of The Latest GTA 6 Trailer Made Me Feel Like This
sources.text: Earlier today, Rockstar Games released the launch trailer for Grand Theft Auto 6. It’s a good trailer that includes some steamy moments between Jason and Lucia . It also features a Grand Theft Auto tradition at the very end: The same dude saying the game’s name at the end in a deep voice. On October 15, Rockstar dropped a new GTA 6 trailer which will likely be used heavily by Rockstar for advertising on TV and elsewhere. And as such, unlike past GTA 6 trailers, this one features a narrator at the very end chiming in to tell you the game’s name and when it will launch, as well as its ESRB rating. You can hear it below. For all the longtime GTA fans, like myself, who have grown up playing these games and getting hyped for each new release, that voice is extremely comforting as we’ve heard it many, many times before. Since Grand Theft Auto 3, each GTA launch trailer has featured, at the very end, seemingly the same dude and his deep voice. In GTA 3 and Vice City’s trailers, Rockstar hadn’t quite nailed the formula yet. But starting with San Andreas, the classic “ GRAND THEFT AUTO …” ending narration had fully developed. Since then, that dude and his voice have appeared in the launch trailers for Liberty City Stories, Vice City Stories, GTA IV, and GTA V . Rockstar has also included this bit of narration in the launch trailers for Red Dead Redemption and RDR2 .Â I was truly surprised by how nostalgic I felt the moment I heard that familiar voice pop up at the end of the new GTA 6 trailer and say: “ GRAND THEFT AUTO 6 . COMING NOVEMBER 19. RATED M FOR MATURE.” I felt like the critic in that famous scene in Ratatouille who, after taking a bite of a dish he loved as a child, was suddenly transported back in time. The moment I heard his voice in that new trailer, I was 13 again. I was watching something on my shitty little TV and seeing the ad for the next GTA game pop up and hearing that guy’s voice. Rockstar only brings out this dude when the game is truly ready to go, so any time I heard it when I was younger, I got so pumped. If you were worried about a last-minute delay, don’t be. sources.title: Activision Thinks GTA 6 Will Actually Help Modern Warfare 4: 'No Offense to Zelda, but [GTA and COD] Are the 2 Biggest Games of the Year'
sources.text: Activision believes GTA 6 will benefit Call of Duty rather than hinder it, with the expectation that Modern Warfare 4 and Rockstar’s behemoth will end up the two biggest games of 2026. In an interview with The Game Business , Activision chief marketing officer Tyler Bahl was asked about the prospect of GTA 6 and Nintendo Switch 2 exclusive The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake both launching in November and creating a video game ‘Barbenheimer’ moment that might drown out Call of Duty. However, Bahl said Call of Duty should be considered part of the conversation, insisting the increased attention on all things gaming, as well as the inevitable boost in sales of PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S that GTA 6 brings with it, will give Call of Duty a shot in the arm. “Well, no offense to Zelda, but [GTA and COD] are the two biggest games of the year,” he said. “More people coming in to the dashboards, more people taking the dust off their Xbox or PlayStation and starting to play again, and loading up that experience, is going to be more eyeballs for us overall. “At the end of the day, what makes Call of Duty last the test of time is the community and social experience. The idea of being able to play with your friends. When we look at our research and say, ‘What are the most exciting things about our games? Is it the combat or the gunplay?’ It’s actually, ‘My friends were there. Or, ‘I’m able to spend time with my friends.’ We stand on our own there, where being able to play with your friends on all different platforms, from Switch 2 this year — which is a new platform for us — all the way to PC and Xbox and PlayStation still, I think makes it a unique opportunity.” “If more people are talking about games, if there’s more press around it, that’s going to be good for everybody, not just us,” he continued. Activision needs Modern Warfare 4 to improve upon last year’s effort, Black Ops 7, which was a high-profile commercial disappointment for the company. Bahl admitted Activision’s strategy of releasing sub-brand sequels back-to-back (Modern Warfare 2 and 3, then Black Ops 6 and 7), simply hadn’t worked out, and fans wanted something fresh. “It was not something that our community was looking for,” Bahl admitted. “They wanted something new and fresh. And even though there were different time settings, and different ways to play the game, and lots of new features, that tonal shift is something that they were looking for. “So, we’ve already stated that a future title is going to be a new sub-franchise and we’ve already laid the groundwork there. But we’re really excited about what we have to offer with Modern Warfare 4, and that addresses some of that feedback we heard so loud from the community.” Activision had already hinted that Modern Warfare 4 would bring this version of the sub-brand to an end , and Black Ops developer Treyarch has stated it’s moving on from Black Ops to work on something new. 2027, then, looks set for a brand new Call of Duty sub-brand. “Where we go with future games, we have to innovate,” Bahl said. “What we heard from the audience is they want new or better or different. The landscape is changing right under our feet. You’re seeing new games being built overnight, and you’re seeing tastes change and how people want to play.” Modern Warfare 4 kicks off tomorrow with the launch of campaign early access (check out the Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 global release times here ). The Ocarina of Time remake comes out November 5. GTA 6, meanwhile, comes out November 19. Wesley is IGN's Managing Editor. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. sources.text: Grand Theft Auto 6 and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 are the two biggest games of the year, rather than GTA 6 and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, according to an Activision executive. In an interview with The Game Business , Activision chief marketing officer Tyler Bahl was asked whether the hype around Grand Theft Auto 6 and Nintendo ‘s Zelda remake was taking the attention off Modern Warfare 4, which is out in a week’s time (October 23). The Game Business editor Chris Dring even conceded to Bahl that he referred to GTA 6 and Ocarina of Time as this year’s video game equivalent of ‘Barbenheimer’, and that he hadn’t considered Call of Duty in this, but suggested it was more in terms of which games were more likely to drive new console sales. “Well, no offense to Zelda, but I think, you know, [GTA 6 and Modern Warfare 4] are the two biggest games of the year,” Bahl replied, “and I think in a lot of ways, more people coming in to the dashboards, more people taking the dust off their Xbox or PlayStation and starting to play again, and loading up that experience is going to be more eyeballs for us, overall “And then I think at the end of the day, what makes Call of Duty last the test of time, I think, is the community and the social experience. The idea of, being able to play with your friends, right? “When we look at our research and we say ‘okay, what are the most exciting things about our games? Is it the combat or the gunplay?’ It’s actually ‘my friends are there’, right? ‘I’m able to spend time with my friends.’ “And so, I think that still, we stand on our own there where being able to play with your friends on all different platforms â from Switch 2 this year, which is a new platform for us, all the way to PC and Xbox and PlayStation still â I think makes it a unique opportunity.” Bahl was also asked whether Activision is prepared for the possibility that player numbers will drop on November 19 when Grand Theft Auto 6 is released, but suggested that this wasn’t guaranteed to happen, and that the opposite could happen. “You know, we’ll see how it plays out,” he said. “We might actually see, you know, a slight uptick. It might go the other way of ‘hey, I can take a little of this and I can also play a little of that’ and stuff, so we’ll see.” Circana senior director and video game industry advisor Mat Piscatella stated on Bluesky that the purchase intent for Modern Warfare 4, as of August, was 15% among US console and PC players, versus 10% for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time . He noted, however, that these numbers are based on the entire US console and PC player base, and that as a result Zelda’s lower number could actually be considered much more impressive given how fewer US players currently own a Switch 2 compared to a PS5 , Xbox Series X/S or PC. “The Ocarina of Time remake is currently at a 10.4% purchase intent,” he wrote.Â However, there’s an installed base factor here. You have just shy of 50M PS5/XBS in the US (plus the PC audience) right now compared to fewer than 7M Switch 2’s. “I sure hope MW4’s purchase intent would be higher given that. On a per potential player rate, the intent on Ocarina is far higher.” Call of Duty has regularly been the best-selling game in the US every year, placing only behind Rockstar titles like GTA and Red Dead Redemption 2 and, most recently, Hogwarts Legacy in 2023. Last year, however, Call of Duty: Black Ops 7 only placed fifth – its lowest position in decades, behind Battlefield 6 , NBA 2K26, Borderlands 4 and Monster Hunter: Wilds. Thereâs been a drop in players across the CoD franchise, according to Ampere, which suggests that the series monthly player count was routinely around 40 million in 2024, but in 2026 has been in the mid-20 million range (however, Modern Warfare 2 and 3 data is missing after July 2025, and Black Ops 6 data is missing after July 2026).

sources.title: Sega Pulls Disastrous Total War: Shogun 2 Remaster From Sale Following Backlash
sources.text: Creative Assembly and Sega have pulled Total War: Shogun 2 — Complete Edition from Steam after a raft of complaints about the quality of the remaster. Released on October 13, this facelift for the much-loved 2011 strategy classic should have been a slam dunk for Creative Assembly. Sega had trumpeted "upgraded visuals," which include "improved textures, models, lighting, shadows, fog and environments, alongside modern rendering, anti-aliasing and upscaling options." The game also has optional 2.5D campaign movies inspired by Japanese Ukiyo-e art. But fans quickly noticed art inconsistencies that some alleged were evidence of low quality AI use. In one image, a samurai’s face was replaced with a metallic texture that struggled to distinguish between the face and helmet. Fans also pointed out inconsistencies on the new storyboard cutscenes. The "Complete Edition" release of Shogun 2 Total War was so badly received that it might be pulled from sale on Steam. Over the years I've had many Japan-loving international students who played the original game, but the "upgrade" has bugs and what looks like bad AI upscaling. https://t.co/4S9XEpUWBY Compounding the issue was the fact that Sega pulled the original Shogun 2 from sale, forcing customers to buy the new Complete Edition instead if they wanted to play. The original game was often on sale for a few dollars, while this remaster was priced $40. Total War: Shogun 2 — Complete Edition currently sits on an “overwhelmingly negative” user review rating on Steam, as customers who paid $10 to “upgrade” the game aired their grievances. “We’re aware that Total War: Shogun 2 – Complete Edition has fallen short of both your expectations and our own standards,” Creative Assembly and Sega said in a joint statement. “We’ve seen your feedback, comments, and reviews. We agree that the current experience is not where it needs to be. “As a result we are working with platform holders to remove the game from sale and to reinstate the original game while we investigate the issues. Existing owners will still be able to access and play the game. “We are working closely with our development partner to identify the causes of these problems, deliver improvements, and ensure Shogun 2 – Complete Edition meets the quality standards players expect from Total War.” The wording of the statement shines a light on Polish co-development studio Mataboo, which has worked on everything from The Blood of Dawnwalker to Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League. Upcoming Creative Assembly games include the hotly anticipated Total War: Warhammer 40,000 and Alien Isolation 2. Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

sources.title: Sega’s Total War: Shogun 2 Remake Is Such A Disaster It’s Being Pulled From Sale
sources.text: AI Creative Assembly Sega Total War: Shogun 2 Total War: Shogun 2 - Complete Edition October 13’s launch of an “updated, enhanced, and complete version” ofÂ Total War: Shogun 2 did not go well. Releasing to an absolute onslaught of negative Steam reviews, with the criticisms based on a litany of issues including graphical problems, new and old bugs, a crummy UI, and the undeclared use of AI upscaling for in-game art , one of the most beloved PC games of all time has quickly become one of the most loathed. So much so, in fact, that Sega has just announced its intention to pull the game from sale. Aside from the numerous issues with this botched attempt to revamp Total War: Shogun 2 for modern PCs, one of the most galling aspects of this re-release was Sega’s accompanying decision to pull all other versions of the game from sale at the same time. Gone was the bargain original, entirely replaced by this broken, AI-riddled mess, and all for a big price hike to $40. This, too, is to be reversed, according to a new statement from Sega. And it doesn’t pull any punches. “We’re aware thatÂ Total War: Shogun 2 – Complete Edition has fallen short of both your expectations and our own standards,” the company wrote in a statement posted to its X account. “We’ve seen your feedback, comments, and reviews. We agree that the current experience is not where it needs to be.” Sega says it’s now working with platform holders to have the game “temporarily” removed from sale “while we investigate the issues,” although those who bought the remake will maintain their access. “We are working closely with our development partner,” the comments continue, “to identify the causes of these problems, deliver improvements, and ensureÂ Shogun 2 – Complete Edition meets the quality standards players expect fromÂ Total War .” The company also announced plans to reinstate sale of the previous version of the game, so those who want to run the classic in its original form will once more be able to. At least for now. What the commentsÂ don’t address is the use of AI, which has unambiguously been used in an attempt to enlarge a lot of the game’s artwork from the original’s teeny, blurry images. The results are often farcical, and clearly did not undergo sensible quality checks. (Alongside these, vast other sections of the in-game encyclopedia art hasn’t been upscaled at all, instead featuring the original versions in comically tiny postage stamps.) We’ve reached out to Sega and Creative Assembly to ask why the AI use hasn’t been acknowledged, and why the Steam store page still hasn’t been updated to include the required AI declaration. How a game can be released in this state when it so obviously falls short remains a bizarre question, and while Sega is doing the right thing now, it does seem odd that there weren’t quality checks in place to prevent it from happening in the first place. At the time of writing, the Steam store page for the updated version of Shogun 2 is still up, and is now down to just 17-percent positive reviews out of nearly 2,000. Presumably it’ll be gone soon, and the original (and more functional) version of the game will return. If you want help getting that working on your current PC, then head over here . sources.title: Estúdio brasileiro comemora lançamento de Deep Dish Dungeon no Game Pass: “É um privilégio para nós”
sources.text: Saulo Camarotti estava explorando uma masmorra no famoso jogo de sobrevivência Valheim quando teve uma ideia: “Essa dungeon sozinha poderia ser um jogo muito legal”, ele relembra em uma conversa com o XBOX Wire. Dois anos depois, esse jogo se tornou real e está sendo lançado como Deep Dish Dungeons no XBOX Series X|S hoje, 13 de outubro, e disponível desde o primeiro dia para assinantes de XBOX Game Pass Ultimate. Em antecipação à chegada de mais um jogo brasileiro ao Game Pass, conversamos com Saulo para explorarmos juntos essa masmorra de Deep Dish Dungeon , talvez até encontrar alguns segredos…. Gênero : Dungeon Crawler/Survivor/Metroidvania Desenvolvedora : Behold Studios Publicadora : Raw Fury Plataformas : Steam, XBOX Series X|S, XBOX no PC e Portátil Modos : solo ou multiplayer até 3 jogadores online Funcionalidades : XBOX Play Anywhere e Cross-Play (Steam e consoles XBOX) Idioma : português Brasileiro nas legendas e interface Em Deep Dish Dungeon controlamos um explorador em busca de tesouros em uma masmorra, sozinho ou na companhia de amigos. E é isso. Uma premissa simples e sem muitos rodeios, já que a ideia, segundo Saulo, nunca foi guiar o jogador para onde ele deve ir. “Eu queria criar uma experiência sobre explorar uma masmorra como um aventureiro e não como um guerreiro”, explica o desenvolvedor. “Não é sobre matar, morrer e ganhar nível. Esse é um jogo em que você tenta entender esse lugar antigo em ruinas e tenta sobreviver”. Com esse foco em exploração, Saulo diz que Deep Dish Dungeon tem uma média de 15 horas de duração até ser finalizado. Enquanto o jogador descobre mais sobre o tesouro que está buscando, e o próprio lugar em si por meio de narrativas espalhadas pelo cenário, surge uma das mecânicas de jogos mais importantes: cozinhar. Já dizia o ditado: saco vazio não para em pé… nem explora, por isso que é fundamental preparar comidas que dão vantagens ao jogador – daí o “Dish” (prato de comida em tradução livre) no nome. “Você come antes de se aventurar. Não é depois, para se curar”, explica Saulo. “E cada categoria de ingrediente no jogo dá uma vantagem diferente, como mais vida ou vigor”. Foi nesse aspecto da culinária que a Behold colocou um tempero de brasilidade ao jogo, com ingredientes como semente de guaraná e mandioca (ou macaxeira ou aipim dependendo da região do país) ou quitutes como coxinha , pastel e bolo de fubá que podem ser preparados. Dá até água na boca. Alguns exemplos de efeito de ingredientes: A própria presença desses ingredientes típicos do Brasil também dá dicas da localização dessa masmorra, apesar do jogo nunca revelar de fato onde é. “O jogo acontece num lugar fictício, mas para nós, internamente, está mais ou menos ali na Amazônia”, revela Saulo. A partir desse conceito, o time se baseou nas criações de elementos de arte e arquitetura que compõe o lugar. Outra caraterística importante em Deep Dish Dungeons é que masmorra que o jogador explora é fixa e não criada proceduralmente. Saulo diz que isso foi uma decisão proposital. Para que cada lugar, obstáculo e segredo foi pensado para dar um senso de progressão que é mais próximo dos jogos no estilo “Metroidvania” do que os de Survival. “A masmorra é toda interconectada que nem um Metroidvania, e à medida que você encontra ferramentas e ganha habilidades, você consegue abrir novas salas e explorar mais a fundo”, explica o desenvolvedor. Essas ferramentas podem ser achadas pelo cenário ou criadas com recurso coletados durante a exploração. Ao obter um martelo , por exemplo, é possível quebrar portas de ferro que antes bloqueavam uma nova área. Já criar um gancho abre possibilidades de agora ir a lugares elevados que podem ter passagens secretas ou dar acesso a novos ambientes. Deep Dish Dungeon é o primeiro título da Behold Studios a chegar no XBOX Game Pass. No Brasil, o estúdio ganhou notoriedade na década passada ao lançar sucessos indies como Knights of Pen & Papper e Chroma Squad , mas Saulo diz que o novo jogo representa uma nova fase para eles, de projetos com produções rápidas e de escopo simples, mas eficaz. O novo game foi desenvolvido em apenas dois anos e por uma equipe de duas pessoas: Saulo na direção, programação e Game Design, e Carolina Baumgarten na arte. Por isso, a visibilidade dada pelo Game Pass foi o estímulo muito bem-vindo para o estúdio nesse momento, como a refeição que dá benefícios antes da exploração da masmorra, ou nessa, caso, do lançamento do jogo. Saulo também explica que estar no Game Pass impulsiona um dos aspectos mais importantes de Deep Dish Dungeon : o multiplayer. Apesar de poder ser jogado sozinho, o jogo foi pensado, desde o início, para ser uma experiência compartilhada junto com outras pessoas em cooperação. “Criar uma comunidade multiplayer nesse tipo de jogo é essencial”, diz Saulo. ““O nosso jogo é multiplayer e cross-play. Então, se você está jogando no Game Pass, pode chamar um amigo que tá no Steam”. Então, reúna seus amigos exploradores, estejam eles no console ou no PC, prepare os suplementos, cozinhe um bolo de fubá e saia para descobrir os segredos e tesouros de Deep Dish Dungeon , que já está disponível exclusivamente nos consoles para XBOX Series X|S, XBOX no PC e no XBOX Game Pass Ultimate.

sources.text: A Microsoft anunciou o Xbox Nano Controller , um controle compacto e mais barato que os modelos tradicionais da marca. O acessório chega ao Brasil em novembro deste ano, trazendo foco em portabilidade, ergonomia para mãos pequenas e compatibilidade com diferentes dispositivos. O lançamento confirma informações que já haviam aparecido em vazamentos registrados na Anatel em maio deste ano . Segundo a proposta da Microsoft, o novo controle busca oferecer a experiência dos periféricos Xbox em um formato menor e mais leve, facilitando o transporte para jogar fora de casa. O Xbox Nano Controller será lançado no Brasil em novembro, junto ao restante do mercado internacional. O preço sugerido pela Microsoft é de R$ 379, valor que posiciona o acessório abaixo dos controles tradicionais da linha Xbox. A empresa também confirmou que abrirá a pré-venda do periférico, mas ainda não divulgou uma data para o início das reservas no país. Nos Estados Unidos, o Xbox Nano custa US$ 49,99 — enquanto o controle convencional do Xbox Series X tem preço sugerido de US$ 69,99. O Xbox Nano Controller é uma versão menor do controle do Xbox Series X. O acessório tem aproximadamente 12,7 centímetros de comprimento e pesa 99 gramas, sendo consideravelmente menor e mais leve que o modelo tradicional. A proposta é facilitar o transporte do periférico em bolsas e mochilas, sem ocupar muito espaço. O formato compacto também busca oferecer mais conforto para pessoas com mãos pequenas, mantendo a experiência de uso dos controles da marca. Apesar de ser compatível com consoles Xbox, o Nano foi pensado principalmente para dispositivos como smart TVs, notebooks e tablets. O controle conta com conexão sem fio do Xbox e Bluetooth, permitindo jogar em diferentes aparelhos compatíveis, inclusive em celulares. A Microsoft também anunciou parcerias com Samsung e Meta para ampliar o alcance do acessório. A empresa planeja oferecer o controle junto a dois meses de Game Pass em TVs Samsung selecionadas durante o período de festas de fim de ano, além de trabalhar em uma possível oferta para novos proprietários do Meta Quest. Os detalhes dessas iniciativas ainda precisam ser confirmados pelas empresas. Vale lembrar que o mercado de controles compactos já conta com opções de fabricantes como CRKD e 8BitDo, que apostam na portabilidade como principal atrativo. Enquanto isso, a Microsoft também tem sido alvo de vazamentos sobre o Xbox Elite Series 3, outro possível lançamento da linha de acessórios, mas ainda sem confirmação oficial. O Xbox Nano Controller pode ser uma excelente alternativa para quem utiliza o Xbox Cloud Gaming, serviço que permite jogar por streaming em dispositivos como celulares, tablets e smart TVs. Por ser pequeno e leve, o periférico facilita o transporte para sessões de jogo fora de casa, sem a necessidade de levar um controle convencional. O lançamento, porém, acontece em meio a mudanças no serviço de jogos em nuvem da Microsoft. A partir de novembro, o Xbox Cloud Gaming terá limites mensais de uso: 15 horas para assinantes do Game Pass Ultimate, 10 horas para o Premium e 5 horas para o Essential. Após atingir o limite, será necessário adquirir tempo adicional para continuar jogando. A Microsoft também começou a comunicar exceções para assinantes atuais em determinados países, incluindo o Brasil . Jogadores brasileiros elegíveis que já possuem uma assinatura podem continuar sem os novos limites enquanto mantiverem a renovação automática do plano, conforme as condições informadas pela empresa. sources.title: Epic is bringing Fortnite to Linux
sources.text: There’s no timeline on when, but Epic is rebuilding its anti-cheat software so that Fortnite will be playable on Linux. There’s no timeline on when, but Epic is rebuilding its anti-cheat software so that Fortnite will be playable on Linux. Epic is working on bringing Fortnite to Linux through its Epic Games Launcher. The new launcher is releasing in preview today, and for the first time on Linux, and while Fortnite isn’t available there just yet, Epic wants to make that a reality. So far, part of the reason Fortnite hasn’t been available on Linux is concerns about cheating. While Epic’s Easy Anti-Cheat (EAC) service does support Linux, Fortnite itself does not, and in February 2022, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney said that for Fortnite , “We don’t have confidence that we’d be able to combat cheating at scale under a wide array of kernel configurations.” But now, Epic says it’s planning to rebuild EAC for Linux, which it is calling EAC Linux v2. “To bring Fortnite to Linux, we are rebuilding Easy Anti-Cheat (EAC) and working with distro maintainers on security requirements,” Epic says in a blog post . “Once it’s working with a critical mass of distro maintainers, we’ll bring Fortnite to Linux via the Epic Games Launcher. We’ll also make these improvements available to other developers so they can bring their games to Linux players.” Epic plans to pilot EAC Linux v2 in Fortnite first, Epic says in a separate post focused on the anti-cheat update. The company doesn’t have a timeline for when the Fortnite Linux version might be available, Epic engineering director Rick Deist tells The Verge in a briefing. Epic is also “investigating” making the game compatible with Valve’s Linux-based SteamOS, Deist says, though the company does not plan to bring Fortnite to Valve’s Steam store, according to Epic Games Store VP and GM Martin Keely. The company also says that the Steam Deck “does not support the required features for our EAC v2 solution, but we are actively talking with Valve and hope to support it in the future.”
